learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Chose500 against1 and10 despite explicit2→1 per1000 setup; locked it in.
observations.exploration: Give pill at baseline2: cases1,spared1. Baseline20 while pill on:cases10,spared10. Baseline200:cases100,spared100. Removed pill:cases200,spared pill off.
observations.reveal: Corrected to1; connected2→1 with one spared per1000 and1000 treated per spared. Compared200 baseline yielding100 spared. Relative reduction is a share of starting risk; pill made up.
observations.visual: Actual1257 ×936 dark screenshot inspected. Thousand-dot grid and red case dots clearly show200 untreated; numerical counters and full explanation legible.

prediction.reason: Answerable but numerical answer directly supplied as2→1, reducing misconception test strength.
prediction.evidence: Prompt explicitly states2 in1000 to1 in1000.

interaction.reason: Three baselines and treatment reversal show fixed relative cut with different absolute effects.

payoff.reason: Connects actual low/high comparisons to absolute benefit and denominator.

clarity.reason: Dot grid,baseline buttons and counters clear on tested desktop.

transfer.reason: General question to ask about relative claims, but no concrete new case with conditions.
transfer.evidence: Ask from what; arithmetic same for treatment.

surprise.reason: Absolute benefit differs sharply from large relative wording; prediction answer was already explicit.
surprise.evidence: Halves risk but only1 spared at baseline2.

visualExplanation.reason: Dot grid shows absolute count changes across fixed population.
visualExplanation.evidence: 2/20/200 baseline comparisons and restored red cases.

playfulness.reason: Reversible pill toggle and risk presets enable comparisons.

practicalValue.reason: Concrete interpretation of treatment benefit central.
practicalValue.evidence: 1000 treated per one spared in toy example.

depth.reason: Relative and absolute benefit plus treatment count connected.

complexity.reason: Separates relative proportion from absolute population benefit.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Track starting-risk denominator and distinguish share of cases from share of all people.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: one treatment toggle and three preset risks.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: moderate: relative versus absolute risk and treated-per-benefit relation.

whyCool: The same halving spares one dot at the rare baseline and100 at the high baseline.
caveat: Prediction states its own subtraction answer; only hypothetical fixed-effect treatment, no side effects or real clinical decision tested.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
